title: MiniMax H3 short-drama episode storyboard
description: Input for scripts/validate_episode.py and scripts/build_prompts.py. Asset references in text use {asset_id} placeholders; <Subject N>/<Picture N> labels are assigned at build time in wiring order (characters, scene, props, then audio).

style.description: Opening style sentence reused by every segment unless overridden

identity_phrase.description: Invariants only (age, bone structure, hair, outfit colours); reused verbatim in every segment

reference_images.description: face, outfit/full body, optional detail; paths relative to this JSON

voice_reference.description: 2–15 s clean speech; attached only in segments where the character speaks

description.description: Written once, pasted unchanged; no people

reference_images.description: A prop without an image WILL be invented by the model

rarity.description: UI tier overlaid in post, never rendered

duration.description: Seconds; snapped to the 17k+5 frame grid at build time

continuity.description: State inherited from the previous segment (positions, props held, light); must not be empty after segment 1. Write "@observed" (optionally followed by wardrobe / light notes) to open from where the previous segment's ACCEPTED take really ended: build_prompts.py then inserts that segment's observed_end_state, and refuses to build until it exists (--allow-planned for drafts)

end_state.description: Named end state for the next segment; no trailing period needed

accepted_take.description: The take that was accepted for this segment; written by observe_take.py

observed_end_state.description: Where the accepted take really ends, read from its last frames (never copied from end_state). Same style as end_state, {asset_id} placeholders

observation_confidence.description: How sure the frames make the observer; low triggers a validator warning

accepted_deviations.description: What differs from the planned end_state and was accepted anyway

negatives.description: Appended verbatim to the description. Write it as a positive lock sentence (e.g. the corridor stays empty), never as a bare 'no X'

start.description: Seconds within the segment; shot 1 must be 0; each shot ≥ 1.2 s

camera.description: One dominant move in official vocabulary, as a sentence

action.description: ≥ 8 words, starting state → movement → ending state, ends with a period

lens.description: Optional focal length / depth of field, e.g. '35mm, shallow depth of field'

lighting.description: Optional per-shot key light direction, colour temperature, practicals; inherits the scene when empty

performance.description: Optional trigger -> reception -> one primary response -> settled; ≤3 observable cues per beat

sound_cue.description: Optional single diegetic sound tied to an action in this shot

end_hold.description: Last shot of the segment: settle 0.5 s then hold 1 s (trimmed at assembly)

first_frame_prompt.description: i2va/fl2va only: English still-image prompt for the shot's literal first frame (see assets/image-prompts.md)

stagings.description: Optional. Opening positions for a scene: one entry per scene visit, bound to the first segment of that visit. build_prompts.py turns it into one fixed blocking sentence at the start of that segment, so positions are stated the same way every time. Later segments in the scene inherit through continuity / "@observed".

segment.description: id of the first segment of this scene visit

character.description: character id; only people present when the scene opens (who enters later is not listed)

at.description: what they are next to, as a phrase that follows the verb: "at the left end of the grey sofa", "by the door". Use things the scene master actually shows

side.description: side of the frame in the scene's main camera axis

posture.description: a verb in the third person: stands / sits / kneels / leans / crouches / lies

others.description: a positive statement about the rest of the space: "the other seats stay empty"
